The service runs as one container of one Deployment, reached through one Service, configured from one
ConfigMap and from a Secret the overlays generate, and patched by two overlays. Everything on this page
is read from those manifests and from the build that produces the image; nothing here is a
recommendation.

| Fact | Value |
|---|---|
| Image | `shopping` |
| Image tag | `latest` |
| Base image | `eclipse-temurin:25-jdk` |
| Container port | `8080` (TCP) |
| Service | `ClusterIP`, port `80` to container port `8080` |
| Replicas | 1 |
| Image pull policy | `IfNotPresent` |
| JVM flags | `-XX:+UseZGC`, `-XX:MaxRAMPercentage=75` |

: Image, port and service of the deployment.


The image carries the OpenTelemetry agent and a Java runtime. The container filesystem is read-only,
the process runs as a non-root user, privilege escalation is disabled, all capabilities are dropped,
and an empty `tmp` volume is the only writable path. The base manifest declares those settings and
both overlays repeat them, so a strategic-merge patch is read by a scanner as the pod it merges into.

<!-- evidence: services/shopping/k8s/base/deployment.yaml:24, services/shopping/k8s/base/deployment.yaml:145, services/shopping/k8s/overlays/dev/deployment-patch.yaml:16, services/shopping/k8s/overlays/dev/deployment-patch.yaml:30, services/shopping/k8s/overlays/k3d/deployment-patch.yaml:18 -->

| Resource | Request | Limit |
|---|---|---|
| `cpu` | `250m` | `1` |
| `memory` | `768Mi` | `1.5Gi` |

: Resource requests and limits of the base container.


The base container is sized for a cold JVM plus a Liquibase migration on a shared machine. The `dev`
overlay asks for less and caps the container lower as well; the `k3d` overlay declares no resources of
its own and therefore leaves the base values in place.

### 2.1 Environment variables and where they come from

<!-- evidence: services/shopping/k8s/base/deployment.yaml:24, services/shopping/k8s/base/deployment.yaml:145 -->

The container declares 13 environment variables. The connection
details are read from one Secret, the settings from the ConfigMap, and one value is a literal: the
path of the mounted seed, which is how the offer fixture reaches the process.

| Variable | Source | Name | Key or value |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE` | ConfigMap | `shopping` | key `spring-profile-active` |
| `JWT_ISSUER_URI` | ConfigMap | `shopping` | key `JWT_ISSUER_URI` |
| `SHOPPING_BASKET_CURRENCY` | ConfigMap | `shopping` | key `SHOPPING_BASKET_CURRENCY` |
| `SHOPPING_BASKET_DELIVERY_RATE` | ConfigMap | `shopping` | key `basket-delivery-rate` |
| `SHOPPING_BASKET_DELIVERY_FREE_WHEN_SMART` | ConfigMap | `shopping` | key `basket-delivery-free-when-smart` |
| `SHOPPING_BASKET_ESTIMATE_FROM` | ConfigMap | `shopping` | key `basket-estimate-default-days-from` |
| `SHOPPING_BASKET_ESTIMATE_TO` | ConfigMap | `shopping` | key `basket-estimate-default-days-to` |
| `SHOPPING_BASKET_ESTIMATE_ZONE` | ConfigMap | `shopping` | key `basket-estimate-zone` |
| `SHOPPING_BASKET_ESTIMATE_FALLBACK` | ConfigMap | `shopping` | key `basket-estimate-fallback` |
| `SPRING_CONFIG_ADDITIONAL_LOCATION` | literal | — | `file:/etc/shopping/offer-fixture.yaml` |
| `SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL` | Secret | `shopping-db` | key `jdbc-url` |
| `SPRING_DATASOURCE_USERNAME` | Secret | `shopping-db` | key `username` |
| `SPRING_DATASOURCE_PASSWORD` | Secret | `shopping-db` | key `password` |

: Environment variables of the container, with the object each one is read from.


The base ConfigMap declares the keys `JWT_ISSUER_URI`, `SHOPPING_BASKET_CURRENCY`, `basket-delivery-free-when-smart`, `basket-delivery-rate`, `basket-estimate-default-days-from`, `basket-estimate-default-days-to`, `basket-estimate-fallback`, `basket-estimate-zone`, `offer-fixture.yaml`, `spring-profile-active`. Every key the container
reads through a `configMapKeyRef` is one of them; the key that holds a document rather than a value,
`offer-fixture.yaml`, is not an environment variable at all — it is mounted as a file and named by
`SPRING_CONFIG_ADDITIONAL_LOCATION` instead. A key added to the ConfigMap without a matching reference
in the Deployment is dead, and a reference to a key the ConfigMap does not carry stops the pod at
admission.

### 2.2 Probes

<!-- evidence: services/shopping/k8s/base/deployment.yaml:131, services/shopping/k8s/base/deployment.yaml:138, services/shopping/k8s/base/deployment.yaml:124 -->

| Probe | Declared by | Path | Port | Initial delay | Period | Timeout | Failure threshold |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `livenessProbe` | base | `/actuator/health/liveness` | 8080 | — | 10 | 5 | 6 |
| `readinessProbe` | base | `/actuator/health/readiness` | 8080 | — | 5 | 3 | 3 |
| `startupProbe` | base | `/actuator/health/liveness` | 8080 | — | 10 | 3 | 60 |

: Probes that keep the container alive and route traffic to it.


The base manifest declares all three probes, thresholds included: the startup probe owns the cold
start, the liveness probe restarts a container that stopped answering, and the readiness probe takes
it out of the Service. No overlay adds a probe.

### 2.3 Profiles and overlays

<!-- evidence: services/shopping/k8s/base/deployment.yaml:59 -->

| Profile | Activated in |
|---|---|
| named by a ConfigMap key, never stated as a literal | the base manifest, through the key `spring-profile-active` |

: Spring profiles the manifests activate.


<!-- evidence: services/shopping/k8s/overlays/dev/kustomization.yaml:4, services/shopping/k8s/overlays/k3d/kustomization.yaml:15 -->

| Overlay | Namespace | Name prefix | Pull policy | Requests | Limits | ConfigMap keys | Secret keys |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dev` | `shopping-dev` | `dev-` | `Always` | cpu 100m, memory 256Mi | cpu 500m, memory 512Mi | `spring-profile-active`, `JWT_ISSUER_URI` | `jdbc-url`, `password`, `username` |
| `k3d` | `shopping` | none | — | — | — | `spring-profile-active`, `JWT_ISSUER_URI` | `jdbc-url`, `password`, `username` |

: Overlays, the namespace they deploy into and what each one patches.


The `dev` overlay deploys into its own namespace under a `dev-` name prefix and points the datasource
at a database on the local machine. The `k3d` overlay keeps the shared namespace, adds an Ingress and
the Namespace it deploys into, and is the only overlay that declares the telemetry settings; it also
replaces the issuer address the base states with the one Keycloak the shop cluster runs.

<!-- evidence: services/shopping/k8s/overlays/k3d/deployment-patch.yaml:18 -->

|---|---|---|

| `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` | literal | `shopping` |
| `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` | literal | `http://otel-collector:4317` |
| `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL` | literal | `grpc` |
| `OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER` | literal | `otlp` |
| `OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER` | literal | `otlp` |
| `OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER` | literal | `none` |
| `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER` | literal | `parentbased_traceidratio` |
| `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG` | literal | `1.0` |

| `kustomization.yaml`, `dev` overlay | the kustomization that composes the overlay |
| `deployment-patch.yaml`, `k3d` overlay | the patch applied to the Deployment |
| `ingress.yaml`, `k3d` overlay | the Ingress in front of the Service |
| `kustomization.yaml`, `k3d` overlay | the kustomization that composes the overlay |
| `namespace.yaml`, `k3d` overlay | the Namespace the overlay deploys into |

### 2.5 Infrastructure the service depends on

<!-- evidence: services/shopping/k8s/infra/otel-collector.yaml:2 -->

1 manifest describes an object the service uses and no
overlay composes it: the collector that receives the telemetry. It is applied separately from the application
overlay, so an overlay applied on its own brings up a service whose dependencies are assumed rather
than deployed. The database and the token issuer are not in this set at all — the workspace's cluster
skill deploys them, and the overlays only name their addresses.

| Manifest | Objects it declares |
|---|---|
| `otel-collector.yaml` | `ConfigMap otel-collector-config`, `Service otel-collector`, `Deployment otel-collector` |

: Infrastructure manifests outside the application kustomization.
